answer: Sybil mills fail a midnight sight they cannot pre-aim. The applicant bonds 8.70 POA and, after observation terrace 5 posts its open hash, must log a 14-byte seed bearing when the published lamp hits geometric nadir, then score the bearing into a clay slip with a 9-barb iron quill under a 2.1-second flash. Two more slips follow 75 seconds apart. Peers rebuild the three barb patterns from the flash tape and refuse a second sight on that terrace. Cost: 8.70 POA plus one night watch. A pre-scored slip, a copied bearing, or a missed flash burns 56% and closes terrace 5 for seven epochs.
